To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a minimally immunoreactive variant of humanized MAb CC49, which has retained its antigen-binding properties, by grafting the potential SDR of MAb CC249 onto the frameworks of human MAb.
we have developed a humanized variant of MAb CC-49 that retains its antigen-binding properties and shows minimal reactivation with anti-idiotypes in patients' sera.

we have developed a humanized anti-cancer monoclonal antibody (HuCC49 MAb) by grafting its specificity-determining regions onto the frameworks of human monoclonal antibodies, and that the variant of the HuCC49 Mab, which is a potential clinical reagent for cancer diagnosis and therapy, retains its antigen-binding affinity and is minimally immunogenic in patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the humanization of murine monoclonal antibodies for clinical use.
the development of a humanized anti-cancer antibody with minimal immunogenicity.
the development of a humanized antibody for clinical use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
humanization is a very powerful approach to minimize immunogenicity of xenogeneic antibodies and that it is a valuable tool in the design of therapeutic reagents for human use.
the grafting of the SDRs of the xenogeneic MAb onto the human MAb framework is a sufficient strategy for humanization of xenogeneic antibodies.

grafting of the CDRs of a xenogene antibody onto the framework of a human antibody is sufficient to produce a humanized antibody that retains its antigen-binding properties and that grafting of only the SDRs would be sufficient for a xenogene antibody to be humanized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the humanization of xenogeneic antibodies can be accomplished by the grafting of the CDRs or the SDRs onto the frameworks of a human antibody.
grafting the CDRs of a xenogene antibody is necessary to retain its antigen binding properties but grafting only the SDRs may suffice for retaining its specificity.

humanization of xenogeneic antibodies by grafting of the CDRs of a xenogene antibody onto human variable frameworks is a reliable approach to generate a non-immunogenic antibody that retains its antigen binding activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the humanization of a murine antibody by grafting the SDRs of the murine antibody onto the frameworks of human antibody should be sufficient for retaining antigen binding activity of the antibody.
the humanization of an antibody can be achieved by grafting only the SDRs of the antibody onto the human antibody frameworks.
the SDRs of an immunogenic murine MAb are sufficient for grafting onto a human MAb framework for humanization.
